question.prompt:
What is the smallest result that can be obtained by the following process?

• Choose three different numbers from the set \(\{3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17\}.\)

• Add two of these numbers.

• Multiply their sum by the third number.

solutions.explanation:
Separate the possibilities by the number used as the multiplier. For each fixed multiplier, choosing the two smallest other available numbers makes the sum as small as possible.

If the multiplier is \(3\), the smallest result is
\[
3(5+7)=36.
\]
If the multiplier is \(5\), the smallest result is
\[
5(3+7)=50.
\]
If the multiplier is \(7\) or greater, the other two distinct numbers have sum at least \(3+5\), so the result is at least
\[
7(3+5)=56.
\]
These cases cover every allowed multiplier. Since \(36\) is attained using the three different numbers \(3,5,7\), the smallest result is \(\boxed{36}\), choice C.
solutions.title: Choose the multiplier first
